cohort: 23,524 low-risk singleton pregnancies delivered at 39+0 to 44+0 weeks' gestation at a tertiary university-affiliated medical center over a 5-year period
finding: Post-term pregnancy was independently associated with increased risk of NICU admission, respiratory morbidity, and infectious morbidity compared to both full-term and late-term pregnancies.
mod_finding: Women in the post-term pregnancy group had a significantly higher rate of cesarean section compared to the late-term group.
